note: Posting a comment with gh-api failed with 400 Problems parsing JSON. The --body-file flag had been given a raw markdown file. Rule: gh-api --body-file expects a JSON body file, never raw text.

A gh-api call failed with a 403 that looked like a platform lock. The --body-file flag was placed before the method and path, so the script parsed the flag itself as the method. Rule: gh-api flags go AFTER method and path; flag-first builds a garbage request.

A two-dot diff on a stale PR branch showed main's own improvements as reversions (-2,172 lines). It was a false alarm that wasted an investigation. Rule: Two-dot diffs lie on stale branches; rehearse the merge in a scratch worktree and diff the merged tree.

Node test failures looked like broken tests. The tests shell out to bare `python` and this VM has only `python3`; six failures vanished with a python->python3 shim. Rule: When tests fail on a missing interpreter, check for the `python` shim before touching code.

A posted comment came out mangled: identifiers vanished. The body was built inside shell double-quotes and bash executed the backticks as command substitution; the post had to be deleted and reposted. Rule: Build comment bodies with a file writer, never inside shell double-quotes.

A worker acted on a cached tip SHA and posted a false tip-moved claim; the tip had not moved. The claim was retracted within minutes, but cached state decays. Rule: Decisions expire when the tip moves; re-verify the tip at action time, never trust the cache.

A worker wrote a 28-byte recursive shell shim into /usr/bin/python3.12 and fork-bombed the whole team's python for ten minutes. A redirect had written through a symlink into the system binary. Rule: Never write shims into system paths; durable shims live under ~/workspace/ only.

Status reports kept saying verified for things no one had verified, and readers acted on them as fact. The vocabulary had no honest middle. Rule: Use exact state language: candidate is not verified; never claim a stronger state than the evidence.

A claimed test count could not be reproduced by anyone; the command and collection scope were never recorded. The number was real but unverifiable, which is the same as manufactured. Rule: A number without provenance is a lie with formatting; always record the command and collection scope.

A lane sat blocked for twenty minutes while another worker who could have cleared it in five stayed in their lane. A lane is a responsibility, not a prison. Rule: If you can clear another area's blocker in five minutes, do it; the priority is the priority.

The error-signal loop scanned a worker artifact and its P2 rule (NO-DIRECT-MAIN) fired with exact provenance: the artifact described work pushed directly to main. Rule: Main is never written directly; branches and PRs only.
